title: Project Alpha Requirements
content:
Project Alpha Requirements Document

Objective: Build a next-generation customer portal that unifies account management, support ticketing, and analytics into a single web application.

1. User Authentication
- Support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OAuth 2.0
- Multi-factor authentication required for admin roles

- Create, assign, and track support tickets
- Priority levels: Critical, High, Medium, Low
- SLA tracking with automated escalation
- File attachments up to 25MB per ticket

4. Analytics Module
- Usage analytics with 90-day retention
- Funnel analysis for onboarding flow
- Custom report builder with drag-and-drop

5. Non-Functional Requirements
- Page load time under 2 seconds (P95)
- 99.9% uptime SLA
- WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
- Support latest two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge

title: API v2 Migration Guide
content:
API v2 Migration Guide

This guide covers the breaking changes introduced in API v2 and provides step-by-step migration instructions.

Breaking Changes:
1. Authentication: Bearer tokens replace API keys. All requests must include Authorization header.
2. Pagination: Cursor-based pagination replaces offset pagination. Use 'next_cursor' from response.
3. Error format: Errors now return RFC 7807 Problem Details JSON.
4. Rate limiting: Reduced from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Includes Retry-After header.
5. Deprecations removed: /v1/users/list endpoint removed. Use /v2/users with query params.

Migration Steps:

Step 1: Update authentication
  Old: X-API-Key: your_api_key
  New: Authorization: Bearer your_token

Step 2: Update pagination logic
  Old: ?page=2&per_page=25
  New: ?cursor=abc123&limit=25

Step 3: Update error handling
  Old: {"error": "Not found"}
  New: {"type": "not_found", "title": "Resource Not Found", "status": 404, "detail": "User 42 does not exist"}

Step 4: Implement rate limit handling
  Check for 429 status code and respect Retry-After header.

Timeline:
- v1 sunset: March 31, 2026
- v2 GA: January 15, 2026

For questions, contact api-support@example.com

title: Competitive Analysis: CloudSync vs DataBridge
content:
Competitive Analysis: CloudSync vs DataBridge

Overview:
CloudSync and DataBridge are the two leading competitors in the data integration space. This analysis compares their offerings across key dimensions.

Pricing:
- CloudSync: $299/month (Basic), $799/month (Pro), Custom (Enterprise)
- DataBridge: $199/month (Starter), $599/month (Business), $1499/month (Enterprise)
- Our pricing: $249/month (Basic), $649/month (Pro), Custom (Enterprise)

Feature Comparison:

Data Connectors:
  CloudSync: 150+ native connectors
  DataBridge: 200+ native connectors
  Us: 85 connectors (gap: need 50 more by Q2)

Real-time Sync:
  CloudSync: Yes (5-second latency)
  DataBridge: Yes (15-second latency)
  Us: Yes (10-second latency)

Transformation Layer:
  CloudSync: SQL-based only
  DataBridge: SQL + visual drag-and-drop
  Us: SQL + Python scripting

Compliance:
  CloudSync: SOC 2, HIPAA
  DataBridge: SOC 2, GDPR
  Us: SOC 2 (HIPAA in progress)

Strengths to Leverage:
- Our Python scripting is unique and appeals to technical users
- Real-time latency is competitive
- Custom enterprise pricing is flexible

Weaknesses to Address:
- Connector count is significantly behind both competitors
- Need HIPAA certification by Q2
- No visual transformation builder

title: Database Schema Design
content:
Database Schema Design for Customer Portal

Table: users
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  email       VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL
  name        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
  role        ENUM('admin','manager','user') DEFAULT 'user'
  created_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
  updated_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()

Table: organizations
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  name        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
  plan        ENUM('free','basic','pro','enterprise')
  created_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()

Table: tickets
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  org_id      INT REFERENCES organizations(id)
  creator_id  INT REFERENCES users(id)
  assignee_id INT REFERENCES users(id)
  title       VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL
  description TEXT
  status      ENUM('open','in_progress','resolved','closed')
  priority    ENUM('critical','high','medium','low')
  created_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
  resolved_at TIMESTAMP

Table: comments
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  ticket_id   INT REFERENCES tickets(id)
  author_id   INT REFERENCES users(id)
  body        TEXT NOT NULL
  created_at  TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()

Indexes:
  CREATE INDEX idx_tickets_org ON tickets(org_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_tickets_status ON tickets(status);
  CREATE INDEX idx_tickets_assignee ON tickets(assignee_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_comments_ticket ON comments(ticket_id);

Notes:
- Use UUID for public-facing IDs, serial for internal
- Add soft delete (deleted_at) column to users and organizations
- Consider partitioning tickets table by created_at for performance

title: User Interview Findings
content:
User Interview Findings - December 2025

We conducted 12 interviews with mid-market customers (50-500 employees) to understand their pain points with our current analytics module.

Key Findings:

1. Dashboard Customization (mentioned by 10/12)
- Users want to rearrange widgets on their dashboard
- Different roles need different default views
- Request for saved dashboard configurations

2. Export Functionality (mentioned by 8/12)
- CSV export is essential; most use it weekly
- 5 users requested scheduled email reports
- PDF export with company branding requested by 3 enterprise users

3. Real-time Data (mentioned by 7/12)
- Current 15-minute delay is frustrating for support teams
- Operations teams need real-time ticket volume monitoring
- Acceptable latency: under 1 minute for most users

4. Collaboration Features (mentioned by 6/12)
- Ability to share reports with team members
- Commenting on specific data points
- Slack integration for alert notifications

5. Mobile Access (mentioned by 5/12)
- Managers check dashboards on mobile frequently
- Current mobile experience is poor
- Native app not required; responsive web is sufficient

Recommendations:
- Prioritize dashboard customization for Q1
- Add scheduled reports to Q2 roadmap
- Investigate real-time data infrastructure costs

title: Brand Voice Guidelines
content:
Brand Voice Guidelines

Our Personality:
We are knowledgeable yet approachable, professional yet not stuffy. We speak to our users as trusted advisors, not salespeople.

Tone Attributes:
1. Clear - We use simple language. No jargon unless our audience expects it.
2. Confident - We make direct statements. Avoid hedging words like 'maybe' or 'we think'.
3. Helpful - Every piece of content should solve a problem or answer a question.
4. Human - We use contractions, ask questions, and acknowledge challenges.

Do:
- Use active voice: 'You can export reports' not 'Reports can be exported'
- Address the reader directly: 'your dashboard' not 'the user dashboard'
- Be specific: '2-minute setup' not 'quick setup'
- Use sentence case for headings

Don't:
- Use buzzwords: 'synergy', 'leverage', 'paradigm shift'
- Be condescending: avoid 'simply', 'just', 'obviously'
- Use all caps for emphasis
- Make promises we can't keep

Examples:
Good: 'Connect your data sources in three steps.'
Bad: 'Leverage our cutting-edge integration platform to seamlessly onboard your data ecosystem.'

Good: 'Something went wrong. Try again, or contact support if it keeps happening.'
Bad: 'An unexpected error occurred. Please retry the operation.'

title: Incident Postmortem: Database Outage
content:
Incident Postmortem: Database Outage
Date: January 23, 2026
Duration: 2 hours 15 minutes (14:30 - 16:45 UTC)
Severity: SEV-1
Impact: Complete service unavailable for all customers

Timeline:
14:30 - Monitoring alerts trigger: database connection pool exhausted
14:35 - On-call engineer (Dan) acknowledges alert
14:42 - Initial investigation: RDS CPU at 100%, connections maxed at 500
14:55 - Root cause identified: Runaway query from analytics cron job scanning full tickets table without index
15:10 - Killed offending query, connections begin to recover
15:25 - Service partially restored, some requests still timing out
15:45 - Read replica promoted to handle overflow traffic
16:00 - Primary database CPU returns to normal
16:30 - Full service restoration confirmed
16:45 - All-clear issued

Root Cause:
A newly deployed analytics cron job executed a full table scan on the tickets table (2.3M rows) without using the existing indexes. This consumed all available CPU and exhausted the connection pool.

Action Items:
1. Add query execution time limits (5 min max) - Dan - Due Jan 30
2. Add missing index on tickets(created_at, org_id) - Dan - Due Jan 27
3. Implement connection pool monitoring with earlier alerts - Alice - Due Feb 3
4. Require query plan review for all cron jobs - Process - Due Feb 10
5. Add database read replica auto-failover - Dan - Due Feb 15

- Train primary admin on core features
- Deliver onboarding completion certificate

- Share best practices and quick-win recommendations

Phase 3: Value Realization (Days 91-180)
- Quarterly business review with stakeholders
- Present ROI analysis using customer data
- Introduce advanced features and integrations
- Connect with product team for feature requests
- Develop customer into a reference/case study candidate

Phase 4: Renewal and Expansion (Days 181+)
- Renewal conversation 90 days before contract end
- Identify upsell opportunities: additional seats, premium features

- Advocate program invitation

- Login frequency (weight: 30%)
- Feature adoption breadth (weight: 25%)
